summary: Stephen Rudd is an international computational biology leader with more than twenty years of experience spanning molecular biology, bioinformatics, pharmaceutical research, commercial genomics and scientific software. His career combines scientific credibility with product leadership, customer engagement, commercial experience and software engineering. He has repeatedly translated complex biological questions into practical bioinformatics products, services and platforms while building multidisciplinary capability across universities, pharmaceutical companies, national genomics initiatives and biotechnology organisations.
biography: Stephen Rudd builds the organisational and technical capability that turns genomic data into useful scientific decisions. Across more than two decades, he has moved from comparative genomics research and academic bioinformatics leadership into pharmaceutical R&D, national and commercial genomics, sequencing-technology market development, and global bioinformatics product leadership.

At Oxford Nanopore Technologies, Stephen progressed through strategic account management, market development and product leadership to Director, Bioinformatics Product. His remit connects customer insight, scientific applications and software delivery. He guides the roadmap for EPI2ME and its Nextflow-based workflow ecosystem, supporting analysis across cloud and local execution while making sophisticated workflows usable by laboratory scientists and experienced bioinformaticians alike.

Earlier, he established a university bioinformatics core in Turku, applied computational biology within Orion Pharma R&D, led scientific and sequencing capability at Malaysian Genomics Resource Centre, and directed commercial computational biology services at QFAB. These roles share a consistent pattern: listen closely to scientific users, create robust operating models, develop people, and turn repeatable analysis into a platform rather than a one-off intervention.

A classical geneticist with a PhD in molecular biology from the University of East Anglia, Stephen contributed to the first Arabidopsis genome and developed Sputnik, an early comparative plant-genomics platform. That research foundation continues to shape a pragmatic leadership style grounded in scientific evidence, product judgement and respect for the people doing the work.

letter.body: Across academic research, pharmaceutical R&D, national and commercial genomics, and sequencing technology, I have repeatedly built the teams, workflows and product structures needed to make complex analysis operational. At Oxford Nanopore Technologies, I have progressed from strategic account and market development roles into bioinformatics product leadership, guiding EPI2ME and a Nextflow-based workflow ecosystem through close partnership with customers, applications scientists, commercial colleagues and software teams. Earlier roles include establishing a university bioinformatics core, leading scientific capability for national genomics programmes in Malaysia, and directing commercial computational biology services in Australia.
